The 30-year, by a wide margin. At 6% on a $400,000 loan, total interest is about $463,000 over 30 years versus about $208,000 over 15, so roughly 2.2x as much. It's not quite double because the 15-year balance falls faster.

The gap usually widens in practice, since 30-year loans typically carry a higher rate than 15-year loans. The 15-year's cost is a much higher monthly payment (about $3,375 vs $2,398 in this example), so the real trade-off is interest saved versus cash-flow flexibility.
